reference.title: BLS ATUS 2025 Table 3: time spent in primary activities by age
reference.denominator: Average primary-activity hours per diary day for the civilian population in each reported age cohort, including participants and nonparticipants; unless specified, ages 15 and over. Not individual schedules or job-holder-only hours.
reference.spreadLimit: Published cohort means show differences across ages, not within-person or individual dispersion. Raw unpublished/rounded markers are preserved; no missing mean is converted to zero.

work.exposureScope: Every initialized resident, including nonworkers and days without discretionary activation. Exact fixed-roster dated age exposure; no survey weights or civilian/noninstitutional eligibility inferred.
work.comparisonStatus: paid-job-primary-time is a modeled subset; work-related commute/search/other activities are not supplied, so the reference is contextual, never an equality pass
limitations: No ATUS survey weighting/design, matched national age/employment sample, civilian/noninstitutional classification or territorial equivalence.
No complete mutually exclusive diary, commuting, job search, travel-purpose classification or employer/occupation-specific schedule evidence.
Overnight attendance units are dated portions, not completed whole shifts.
Committed on-call/24-hour duty is not automatically ATUS primary paid-work time; sleep/reserve conflicts can produce prototype absence.
No birth/death/migration producer; fixed-roster exposure is rejected if its initialized resident identities or current alive/residency facts change.
ATUS Table 3 age means are not individual schedules, coefficient bounds or within-person spreads.
Only currently captured cumulative category time is normalized. A historical subwindow requires dated numerator counters.

gaps: Attendance is chosen independently for each dated portion of a scheduled shift. workedDays/missedDays/plannedDays count calendar-date segments or diary participation, never completed whole shifts. Overnight continuation and shift-wide absence contracts need a finer occurrence model.

Baseline law and offices: January 2021 laws, officeholder rosters and powers are not reconstructed; later place/government/institution identity records remain opening proxies, with no actual 2021 officeholder count claimed.

Deep past: schools, faith, losses, earlier residences and earlier jobs are absent unless the canonical opening generator establishes them; no event inferred from a trait.
Employer revenue, consumption and household bill counterparties are absent. No cash sink or revenue injection is added.
Household consumption contracts, hiring, employer revenue, demography, elections, and law effects are not implemented; their totals cannot establish realism.
Inherited rotating/cycle calendars are imported only at opening. Same recorded-role timetable copied to added workers does not establish observed roster staggering or realistic company headcounts.
Labor context: no school enrollment, primary care responsibility, pensions, business books or funded public staffing imported; canonical matcher reads the records actually present.
Money: CES nonhousing categories and a hypothetical HUD shelter budget exclude actual tenure, debts, taxes, insurance contracts and medical service bills; no housing contract is invented.
No observed employer-specific shift timetables, holiday/leave calendar, care-school-health constraint coverage or licensed-role qualifications.

Opening peer prior is expanded only for requested people and their generated peer groups; other cohorts remain unexpanded. Reciprocal historical acquaintance and name recognition are generated assumptions. Historical school attendance/existence, current closeness, and continued contact are not verified; no independent network calibration has been completed.
Opening vintage: 2021-01-01 household/population estimates retain later source vintages; no reconstructed 2021 census or migration history.
Quiet outsider work is decided and paid chronologically on scheduled dates, then summarized weekly. An endpoint decision never determines past attendance.
Recorded hourly terms are opening SOC wage proxies, not observed historical contracts. Original average-day job fields stay unchanged.

Recorded work is scored and settled on its scheduled dates; remaining time admits one discretionary scored act per tier activation. Sleep reserve and shift placement remain tunable; education, care, consumption and a complete diary are not modeled.
The opening generator records no known coworkers for the selected player; actual coworkers are in the daily circle, but acquaintance knowledge is not invented.
Unsupported opening workplace/occupation shares remain omitted; unassigned actors are not declared unemployed.
Weekday/cycle placement and finite sleep reserve are tunable, not empirical shift facts.

run/warmup elapsed, initialize, advance, rate and process-memory telemetry
canonicalCapturedResultParity.scope: Every corresponding serialized result, including complete captured worlds and final detailed rows. The normal capture does not serialize full CoreState; this is not a whole-world or full-state hash.

timingComparison.scope: Unchanged prepared input, API/schema5, work flags, player and focus selection; only the two declared knowledge-index source paths differ within the captured core2 manifest and four direct pins. Transitive generation files remain unpinned. Actual rates are read from completed captures.

proofLimits: Normal captures omit complete per-person money, knowledge, relationships, open callbacks and other CoreState tables. Captured-result parity cannot prove equality of those omitted fields.
Latest-work cash violations and retained visibility remain producer aggregate checks, not independent receipt-by-receipt or durable-row replay.
Remaining transitive generation sources are outside the source manifest and are not independently repinned.
Age time-use context, employer funding, schedules, attendance mappings and all existing stopgaps remain unresolved; no realism or civic-drive acceptance follows from parity.
Annual timers exclude generation, summary validation and serialization. Process-lifetime memory does not establish isolated steady-state memory or valid GC attribution.
This archiver runs no world, compiler, test, Git operation or release gate. Existing gate evidence is historical and is not reclassified as passing the revised source.
